title: The Untold Story of Stephen
paragraphs:
The Untold Story of Stephen
The First Christian Martyr Who Saw Heaven Open
Most people remember Stephen for one thing.
That is usually where the story begins and ends.

A brave man.
A tragic death.
A few verses in Acts.
But Stephen's story is far bigger than his execution.
His story is the story of what happens when an ordinary believer becomes so consumed by Christ that even death loses its power.
It is the story of a man who was not an apostle.
Not a famous miracle worker when his journey began.
Not a bestselling author of Scripture.
Stephen was simply a faithful servant.
And yet heaven opened for him in a way that Scripture records for almost nobody else.
His story is not ultimately about dying for Jesus.
It is about seeing Jesus more clearly than everyone around him.
And once you see Christ that clearly, everything changes.
The city is still buzzing from the crucifixion of Jesus.
Some claim He rose from the dead.
The religious leaders are terrified because the movement they thought they buried is growing faster than ever.
Thousands are becoming followers of Christ.
Widows are being overlooked in the daily distribution of food.
The apostles cannot personally manage every need.
So seven men are selected to serve.
"A man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit" (Acts 6:5).
The Kingdom of God often promotes people differently than the world.
Stephen's public ministry began because of private faithfulness.
The Greek text of Acts 6:5 uses the phrase:

πλήρης πίστεως καὶ Πνεύματος Ἁγίου
(plērēs pisteōs kai Pneumatos Hagiou)
"Full of faith and the Holy Spirit."
The word πλήρης (plērēs) means completely filled, saturated, overflowing.
His life had become a vessel overflowing with Christ.
Many believers want the power Stephen had.
Few want the surrender Stephen embraced.
"And Stephen, full of grace and power, was performing great wonders and signs among the people."
God's power is never intended to replace God's character.
The Spirit forms holiness before He entrusts influence.
Stephen became dangerous to darkness because heaven had already transformed his heart.
Members of several synagogues began arguing with Stephen.
Acts says they could not withstand his wisdom.
"They were not strong enough to resist."
Not because Stephen was intellectually superior.
Not because he had better debating skills.
Because truth empowered by the Spirit carries a weight that human arguments cannot overcome.
When God speaks through surrendered people, something happens that logic alone cannot explain.
Unable to defeat him honestly, they turned to false accusations.
The same strategy used against Jesus.
The same strategy often used against God's people throughout history.
Stephen was dragged before the Sanhedrin.
The highest religious court in Israel.
The room was filled with powerful men.
Men who believed they were defending God.
Men who had already rejected God's Messiah.
Men who knew Scripture but missed its Author.
"They saw that his face was like the face of an angel."
Yet the people accusing him appear more troubled than the man facing death.
Because peace is one of the strongest evidences of God's presence.
A person controlled by fear cannot radiate heaven.
Then comes one of the longest sermons in the entire New Testament.
It is one of the most important messages ever preached.
Stephen walks through Israel's entire history.
Again and again he shows a devastating pattern.
Israel repeatedly rejected the very people God sent to save them.
The problem was never God's faithfulness.
At the heart of his message stands a powerful phrase.
The expression comes from Hebrew imagery.
A stiff-necked ox refuses the farmer's guidance.

"You know the Scriptures.
You know the Law.
You know the Prophets.
But your hearts remain resistant to God."
Knowledge without surrender is spiritual danger.
A person can know Scripture and still miss Christ.
Then Stephen delivers the sentence that enrages them.
"Which of the prophets did your ancestors not persecute?"
They are no longer hearing a sermon.
And deep down they know he is right.
Conviction often feels like attack when pride refuses repentance.
Then comes the moment that changes everything.
"But he, being full of the Holy Spirit, gazed into heaven and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God."
Throughout the New Testament, Jesus is normally described as seated at the Father's right hand.
Many scholars have noted the uniqueness of this moment.
Scripture does not explicitly tell us why.
The King rises for His faithful servant.
The Savior welcomes His witness home.
The One Stephen preached now appears before Stephen's eyes.

θεωρῶ τοὺς οὐρανοὺς διηνοιγμένους
(theōrō tous ouranous diēnoigmenous)
For one brief moment the curtain separating earthly suffering and heavenly reality is pulled back.
Stephen sees what everyone else in the room cannot.
But this is where Stephen's story becomes astonishing.
Because as stones crush his body, his heart reveals who truly lives within him.
His final words echo another voice.
"Lord, do not hold this sin against them."

μὴ στήσῃς αὐτοῖς ταύτην τὴν ἁμαρτίαν
(mē stēsēs autois tautēn tēn hamartian)
"Do not charge this sin against them."
Who speaks like that while being murdered?
The miracle of Stephen is not merely that he died bravely.
The miracle is that he loved radically.
And standing nearby was a young man named Saul.
Perhaps unable to forget the face of the man he helped destroy.
The story of Stephen does not end with Stephen.
His death becomes one of the seeds that eventually leads to Saul's conversion.
The greatest missionary in Christian history.
One faithful witness helped change the world.
You may never know what your obedience is accomplishing.
Stephen did not see Paul's future.
The untold story of Stephen is not really about martyrdom.
Everyone in that courtroom saw the same circumstances.
And what you see determines how you endure.
When you see only your pain, despair grows.
When you see only your enemies, bitterness grows.
When you see only your limitations, fear grows.
But when you see Christ, courage grows.
Yet he gained something infinitely greater.
The final thing he saw on earth was hatred.
The first thing he saw in eternity was Jesus.
And suddenly every stone became insignificant.
Maybe you feel attacked for your faith.
Stephen stood alone before powerful opposition.
Stephen remained full of the Spirit.
His story reminds us that God often does His greatest work through people history barely remembers.
And eternity will reveal what faithfulness accomplished.
Because in God's Kingdom, success is not measured by popularity.
And Stephen was faithful until the very end.
The same Jesus who stood to welcome Stephen still welcomes surrendered believers today.
The same Christ who strengthened Stephen still strengthens His people.
The same Lord who opened heaven for Stephen still reigns on the throne.
And one day, every faithful servant will finally see what Stephen saw.
One day every voice that mocked Christ will fall silent, but every eye that longs for Him will finally see Him.
